name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
summary: A hip-hinge exercise using a barbell to build the hamstrings, gluteus maximus, and posterior chain under controlled tension.

setup: Unrack or deadlift the barbell to a standing lockout with feet hip-width apart.
Grip the bar slightly outside your thighs with a double-overhand or hook grip.
Stand tall, brace your core, pull your shoulder blades slightly down and back, and unlock your knees slightly.
steps: Push your hips backward as if reaching for a wall behind you, keeping your shins nearly vertical and knees softly bent at a fixed angle.
Lower the bar in a straight vertical path, skimming closely down your thighs and past your knees.
Descend until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings, typically around mid-shin level, while maintaining a flat, neutral spine.
Drive your hips forward and push through your midfoot to return to the upright starting position, squeezing your glutes at the top.
instructions.breathing: Inhale and brace your core at the top, hold your breath through the descent and turn-around, and exhale as you lock out the hips.
cues: Reach your hips toward the wall behind you.
Paint your legs with the bar.
Keep a soft knee bend and freeze that angle.

common_faults.fault: Rounding the lower back to reach lower to the floor.
common_faults.correction: Stop the descent as soon as your hips stop moving backward and your hamstrings reach full stretch.

common_faults.fault: Squatting the weight down by excessively bending the knees.
common_faults.correction: Keep your shins vertical and focus on horizontal hip travel rather than vertical drop.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the barbell to drift away from the legs.
common_faults.correction: Engage your lats to keep the bar in constant light contact with your thighs and shins.

precautions: Do not sacrifice spinal neutral for extra range of motion.
